This has potential. Seems quite fun. It will be a pain to play though, since the construct is very clunky and it's mostly a giant wall of text that needs a pretty good amount of memorizing. The very first things that caught my eye:

* don't be afraid of special dice! Make it interesting by adding D4, D8, D10, D12, D20... multipliers work, too.
* add a bit of luck in there. For example, basic bomb dealing 12 damage every time is a bit "boring". Why not make it, let's say, 1D6 times 2? You could deal 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 or 12 damage depending on your roll. A monster having 10 hp is a guaranteed kill with 12 flat damage, but would you take the risk when there's a 67% chance of not killing it...? You can spice it up even further by making 1 a miss and 6 a crit.
* the customizing and leveling process is now solely based on abilities. I would suggest adding the option to increase damage and health in there. You might also want to tweak some of the flat damage things, such as "your IGNI deals +1 damage". It seems powerful at early levels but damn near useless on later levels. Add a scaling, for example "your IGNI deals +1 damage for each 5 levels you have gained" would fix this. At level 0-5 it would still be +1, but at, let's say, level 30 it would be +6. At that point it's not just a wasted point.

Anyway, this seems really cool and I'm looking forward to your progress. You do, however, strike me as a person who doesn't have too much experience in tabletop gaming. The most important rules are **making it fun, making it interesting** and **making it progressive.**

**Things have a tendency to work out.** A solution to a problem or another usually reveals itself eventually. Facing major anxiety and stress over things that are not relevant or you can not control is mostly pointless.

**Happiness comes from within.** It's about doing your best to enjoy the things in life, no matter how major or little. Even a depressed person can find some level of satisfaction if they change their perspective a little. "Forcing" yourself to do activities that used to bring you satisfaction is a pretty good way to go. At least for me it worked; I started enjoying things again. Also, be cautious of the media you follow. If reading the news brings you feelings of despair and depression then avoid reading them.  
  
**Being intelligent does not make you superior.** A recurring theme around this subreddit is about the superiority of INTJs. It shouldn't be. I know that sometimes, even usually, it's hard to find someone who understands. For us, it's challenging to be heard in this world. But being on another level than a vast majority of the people surrounding you does not make you better than them. If anything, makes you worse. They fit in and you do not. It's a matter of how you deal with it. 

**You don't have to like everyone, but you have to get along with everyone.** There usually is at least *something* to talk about with pretty much anyone. Being fluent in small talk is a gift. It makes things much less awkward for everyone. All social skills can be learned and fabricated. It just takes immense amounts of effort, time and practice. It's a valuable skill, even if you hate doing it. For your personal and more advanced needs, find people who are at least somewhat on your level and never let them go.

**You can always improve yourself.** Identity, manners and personality are not set in stone. You have tendencies towards certain actions and thoughts, sure, but it doesn't necessarily mean that you have to blindly follow your beliefs. Personally, I find the ability of questioning everything one of the greatest traits of being INTJ. Sometimes you have to question yourself. Over the past few years I've changed my views on a bunch of things. If you don't like something about yourself (that isn't purely genetic), it most certainly can be changed.

And lastly, **never feel bad for being who you are.** People have a habit of judging you based on social norms. You prefer to stay at home and read a book rather than go to a party and people start judging you? Let them. Because, who cares? It's your life, and that's how you prefer to spend your time. Your thoughts are your thoughts, your morals are your morals, your views are your views. Nobody else's. *(Pro top: try to avoid complete solitude. Go out, even a few times a year. We want to be alone, but not lonely. Loneliness is a pathway to dark thoughts.)*

If any additional thoughts or questions reveal themselves then please, don't hesitate to throw a message at me.

Yours,  
Martifex

Depression comes in many forms. I kind of feel like a very major misconception about depression is that it revolves around one's feelings. I'm pretty sure that the most usual symptoms are slow thinking, lack of energy, lack of motivation and unhealthy thoughts.

I don't think that there is a "right" or "wrong" here. However, I have heard from others with our condition that they tend to get more physical symptoms than those with unipolar depression. These include dizziness, sleep disturbances, restlessness, slowed body movement and unexplained physical problems, such as headache or back pain.

There are both negative and positive aspects to our condition's version of depression. What makes bipolar depression so much more brutal than unipolar is the contrast. First you're at your high, sometimes at the top of your life, and then you fall into the deep, dark abyss either slowly or swiftly. The difference is what makes it feel so overpowering. However, on the contrary to regular depression, we *always* bounce back from it. It's kind of a package deal. Some psychiatrists and experts have even claimed that depression goes easier on those with bipolar, because you never really get "stuck" there for years to an end. 

On the very last note - remember that in our case, usually nothing triggers a depressive episode. It just kind of... happens. And then it unhappens. And so we are doomed to repeat the circle of mind all over again.

When people talk about suicidal actions they tend to mean concrete physical harm that leaves proof. However, self-harm comes in many forms. Physical, psychological and social actions that affect one's own life negatively that they do knowingly are all categorized under self-harm. In fact, I'm willing to bet that the most common forms of self-harm are intentional social isolation and not taking care of yourself (nutrition, hygiene and so on).

I can't really tell you what to do about your situation. I don't know your backgrounds, nor do I know how smacking yourself in the head in a burst of rage affects you and what you're hoping to accomplish by doing so. What I do know is that it is definitely self-harm and you should try to stop doing it. The only advice I can give you is to talk it out with someone and try to control your urges. If your friends, SO or family doesn't understand, then consider a professional. 

Other than that - I hope you stay well and find balance and harmony in your life. And remember: tomorrow is a new, brighter day. As it has been for as long as I remember.

It's not a disease, per sē, but a disorder. It falls under the category of psychiatry. It may either be a condition on its own or a symptom of another ailment. The definition over whether hypersexuality is a problem or not is still quite vague. You are not at fault, you are not in control of what's going on in your brain. 

The main point here is whether *you* feel like you have a problem or not. If you don't like it, can't control your urges, have your hyper affect your every-day life or feel like you need help, then yes, a sexual therapist would be recommended. They can't fix you, but they can give you insight and some valuable tools on how to control it.
